1.point: Law, path and truth are not three things but one religion at three depths (the Prophet's words, his way of acting, what he saw), and you reach each depth only by going through the one before it.
steps: Define the law and show it is not kept for its own sake but leads somewhere (to nearness).
Define the path as the inward way of doing the lawful act, which leads to the truth.
Tie the three to the Prophet: words, actions, states (the hadith).
Show that each depth lies inside the previous one, so none can be skipped (ship, sea, pearl).

2.point: Because the inner is reached only through the law, nothing inward can replace the law: wonders without it are magic, the light of knowing God does not come to a heart that drops the law, and the first inner work happens inside the law, as attention in the prayer already prayed.
steps: Someone claiming the truth while dropping the law has left the ship; Kubra: such wonder-workers are liars.
The lie is the claim to know God; the feat is magic, not karama.
Why the law cannot be skipped: it purifies character, and purified character is the way to knowledge of God.
Hence the light of divine knowledge does not descend without the law (Khomeini).
The first inner work therefore sits inside the law: attention in the prayer, beginning at Allahu akbar.

3.point: The law binds to the last breath: the Prophet kept it to the end, so release at a high station is a lie; at the end worship becomes gratitude, and the last stage is lived among people.
steps: State the claim of release and Tabatabaʾi's rejection of it.
His reason: the Prophet kept every precept to the end of his life.
What changes at the end is worship's meaning, from growth to gratitude.
The last stage is lived among people (the four journeys).

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: Defines the law and establishes that it is not an end in itself but leads to nearness, naming the path; first link.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Defines the path as the inward side of the lawful act and names the truth as what the Prophet saw; second and third terms placed.

¶3.label: support
¶3.why: The hadith 'words, actions, states' is the evidence for the three definitions already given in ¶1-2 and is the wording the section's point rests on.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Supplies the 'each only through the one before' step with Kubra's ship, sea, pearl; the point needs this and nothing earlier gave it.

¶5.label: restate
¶5.why: 'Puts the same order without the image': Hamadani and Mutahhari repeat ¶4's claim that the three are one reality at different depths; adds names (shell, core, kernel) but no step.

¶6.label: aside
¶6.why: A second example of one prayer holding all three depths; ¶2 already did this with prayer beside the Prophet, and no later sentence uses khidma, qurb, wusul.

¶7.label: aside
¶7.why: Opens a parallel ladder (islam, iman, ihsan) that the point does not need; an analogy to a step already made.

¶8.label: aside
¶8.why: Completes the islam/iman/ihsan detour and closes with Amuli repeating the order ¶4 established; deleting ¶7-8 loses nothing the argument uses.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: Draws the first consequence: claiming the truth without the law means leaving the ship; Kubra's test for wonder-workers.

¶10.label: advance
¶10.why: Locates the lie in the claim to know God and names the feat magic rather than karama; a step the point states explicitly.

¶11.label: advance
¶11.why: Gives the reason the law cannot be skipped: it purifies character, which is the way into knowledge of God (Bahari).

¶12.label: restate
¶12.why: 'The chain runs in one direction only' re-walks ¶11's order; the traveller who claims release repeats ¶9's claimant.

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: Supplies the point's second clause: the light of divine knowledge does not descend without the law (Khomeini).

¶14.label: aside
¶14.why: Light does not loosen the law once it has come: the converse claim, which belongs to Section 3's point (law to the end), not to this section's.

¶15.label: aside
¶15.why: Forty-day fasting produces experiences anyone can mistake for God; explains why false claims arise but the point does not need it and no later step uses it.

¶16.label: aside
¶16.why: 'Keeping the law is the harder discipline' is a comparison, not a step; ¶17 borrows only the phrase 'lifelong keeping' as a connector.

¶17.label: advance
¶17.why: Delivers the point's last clause: the first inner work is inside the prayer, at Allahu akbar, and attention is what slips.

¶18.label: support
¶18.why: Shows why attention is work (the car, the vicious circle); ¶20 answers this circle, so a later paragraph uses it.

¶19.label: aside
¶19.why: A second authority on attention; the two remedies Khomeini names are not taken up by ¶20 or the point.

¶20.label: restate
¶20.why: 'Gives the practice more depth each time it is done' repeats ¶17; the remembrances are deferred to Chapter Ten rather than used.

¶21.label: advance
¶21.why: States the claim of release and Tabatabaʾi's rejection with the 'beginning to final stage' rule.

¶22.label: advance
¶22.why: Gives the reason: the Prophet kept every precept to the last moments of his life; the point names this.

¶23.label: advance
¶23.why: Introduces the shift in worship's meaning at the end of the road, from growth to something else, setting up the gratitude step.

¶24.label: advance
¶24.why: Lands worship as gratitude and ties it to the chapter's opening Munajat line; the point's third clause.

¶25.label: advance
¶25.why: Supplies the final clause: the last stage is lived among people, via the four journeys.

¶26.label: restate
¶26.why: Summarises all three sections' points in one paragraph; every sentence has already been concluded once.

¶27.label: aside
¶27.why: 'The law is the boundary' restates; 'Who walks beside the traveller?' raises a question this chapter does not answer.
